title: Verdigris Telemed — outbound workbench
content:
Notes to self — Verdigris Telemed (early-stage telehealth platform; primary offering: urgent-care + chronic care virtual visits).

Pocket research (quick hits)
- Founded 2019, Series B (2024) — expanded into employer contracts in 2025.
- Primary markets: West Coast + Midwest; mid-market employers and regional health systems.
- Tech stack: React frontend, Kubernetes-based infra (GKE), Postgres, uses AWS us-west-2 for prod; claims ‘PHI isolated VPCs’ in job listings.
- Existing AI usage: internal rules for triage, note templates, speech-to-text partner (third-party). They advertise faster intake + improved clinician throughput.
- Pain signals: job posts for "clinical workflow automation" & "care-team efficiency"; press about rising clinician burnout.

Who to target (roles)
- Head of Clinical Operations / VP Nursing (clinical champion) — cares about time-to-task, clinician burden, compliance.
- Director of Engineering / Head of Platform (technical champion) — cares about deploy model, latency, infra fit.
- Head of Privacy & Compliance (procurement blocker) — HIPAA, BAA, data residency.

Hypothesis: pilot that replaces/augments triage note drafting + quick code suggestions for clinicians (automated visit summary + structured problem list) could reduce average visit aftercare admin time by ~25–40% and improve throughput per clinician by 10–15%.

Value props to lean on for outreach
- Production-first inference: low-latency summaries so clinicians don’t wait; can run in customer VPC or private deployment to satisfy PHI isolation.
- Predictable economics: dedicated pools to keep token costs bounded for heavy triage volumes; batching + caching suggestions to save $$ while preserving SLOs.
- Auditability & provenance: traceable request logs + model version pinning for clinical audit and QA.
- Rapid pilot: 4–6 week scoped pilot focused on 1–2 clinics, defined evals (time-per-chart, clinician satisfaction NPS).

Sample outbound sequence (short, iterative)
1) LinkedIn connection — 1 sentence reason: "Curious about Verdigris' approach to clinical documentation efficiency — worked with similar telemed teams on inference pilots."
2) Follow-up email (subject ideas below)
   - Subject A: Quick pilot idea to cut clinician admin time at Verdigris
   - Subject B: HIPAA-friendly LLM pilot for telemedicine notes (2–4 week scope)
   Email body (short):
   "Hi <Name>,

   Quick intro — I’m Aisha from Redwood Inference. We help telehealth platforms run clinical-quality inference with private deployments (VPC / on-prem) so PHI stays under customer control. We ran a 6-week pilot with a regional telemed provider and saw ~30% reduction in admin time for clinicians by automating visit summaries + structured problem lists.

   If there’s interest, I can share a one-page pilot plan — low lift for your engineers and scoped to 100–200 visits to measure outcomes. Would it make sense to do a 15-min intro next week?

   Cheers,
   Aisha
"
3) Follow-up 1 week later — short case study snippet + ask for intro to Head of Clinical Ops.

Objection handling (quick responses)
- Objection: "We can’t send PHI to external vendors / no BAA."
  Response: "We offer private deployments (VPC or on-prem) and will sign a BAA; all inference can run in your network with keys you control. We can provide an architecture diagram for your security team and a short security questionnaire response."

- Objection: "Latency + clinician UX — slow model responses will disrupt flow."
  Response: "Pilot uses optimized kernels and routing to keep inference sub-500ms for summaries at typical triage lengths; we can run inference in-region on dedicated capacity for predictable latency and provide per-request traces for debugging UX issues."

- Objection: "Cost — tokens could blow up with high volume visits."
  Response: "We configure batching, prefix caching, and recommend compact quantized model variants for triage workloads to lower unit costs; pilot includes a cost forecast and tuning run to demonstrate achievable per-visit cost."

- Objection: "Clinical accuracy / hallucination risk."
  Response: "We build evaluation harnesses tied to your prompts and gold-label examples and implement guardrails (conservative extractive outputs, human-in-loop review flag). We also support model pinning and audit logs so you can track regressions and rollback."

Pilot plan (sketch)
- Scope: 2 clinics / 100–200 visits over 4–6 weeks.
- Goals: reduce clinician after-visit admin time (target 20–30%), measure clinician satisfaction, and validate safety checklist items.
- Deliverables: infra guide (VPC peering + BAA), small inference endpoint (private), prompt set + evals, weekly sync + final playbook.
- Success criteria: measurable time-per-chart reduction OR 80% positive clinician feedback on summaries AND security signoff.

Quick integration notes for the engineering conversation
- Likely path: Redwood Private deployed into Verdigris VPC (EKS) OR dedicated hosted with VPC peering + strict IAM.
- Data flow: visit audio -> STT partner -> text to inference -> structured summary back to EHR draft. Keep PHI in VPC; only model logits/state live on customer's infra.
- Team ask: 1x backend eng for 2 weeks to wire the callback + 1x infra engineer to review network setup (peering/roles).

Risks / unknowns to validate early
- Where do they currently store transcripts and who has access? (S3? internal DB?)
- EHR integration surface — which fields they want populated (note body vs structured fields).
- Consent model for AI-assisted documentation (clinician opt-in vs default).

Call prep checklist (for first intro)
- Share 1-page pilot plan + security one-pager beforehand (attach).
- Ask: current clinical workload metrics, existing AI usage, security review timeline, decision-making stakeholders, preferred pilot timeline.
- Bring: short demo video (30s) of before/after note generation, anonymized example outputs, cost estimate template.

Next tactical steps (my todo)
- [ ] Draft 1-page pilot plan (due: 2026-02-25) — include cost projection and SLOs.
- [ ] Pull anonymized before/after example from past pilot (ask Maya).
- [ ] Create Slack intro in #enterprise-outreach with quick TL;DR and link to this doc.
- [ ] Identify potential intro at Verdigris (LinkedIn target: Samira Holt — VP Clinical Ops).

Random scratch ideas (brain dump)
- Offer a short "Safety & Review" gating feature in pilot: clinicians can mark generated summary as "Draft OK" or "Needs Edit" — track the fraction of drafts accepted to quantify trust.
- If they care about cost, precompute candidate summarization lengths (short/medium/long) and let clinicians choose default.
- Pre-bake a CSV of structured concepts (problem list, meds, follow-ups) to push to EHR — easier to integrate than free text.

End of notes.

(Keep this doc alive — update with meeting notes, security feedback, and pilot metrics.)
